g.text: Sequences
Sequence(...) plays animations one after another: each one starts when the previous one ends. Pass the
animations in order and, if you want, loop_limit to repeat the whole sequence. A step can be any
animation, including another sequence.
Waiting
Show(duration) keeps the block still for a while, looking exactly as it normally does. Hide(duration) hides
the block for a while. Use them to delay or to separate steps.
Two levels of repetition
A loop_limit on an animation inside the sequence repeats only that animation, every time the sequence
runs. On the sequence, it repeats the whole thing from its first step. For example, a sequence with
loop_limit=2 runs three times, and a Pulse with loop_limit=4 inside it pulses five times in each run.
Steps are not blended
Each step starts from its own starting state, and svgblock does not smooth the connection between steps.
After a RiseIn the block is in place, so a second entrance right after it makes the block jump back to its
starting state and enter again. An exit leaves the block hidden, so a step that starts visible makes it
reappear at once. Choose steps that fit together, and use Show to separate them.
Entering and leaving
A common shape is an entrance, an ambient animation and an exit, such as Sequence(RiseIn(),
Float(loop_limit=3), RiseOut()). An exit ends hidden and an entrance starts hidden, so with
loop_limit=None the sequence starts over without anyone seeing the join. That holds while fade is on:
with fade=False the block would jump from where the exit ended to where the entrance starts.
Infinite steps
• An animation with loop_limit=None never ends, so only the last step of a sequence can be infinite:
anything after it would never play.
• When the last step is infinite, the sequence never reaches its end, so its own loop_limit has no effect.
